title: {si} + present: plans that depend on something (s'il pleut, on va à la bibliothèque)
description: Make a plan that depends on the weather or on someone: {s'il pleut, on va à la bibliothèque}.
can_do: Say what you will do if the weather is nice, wet or snowy: {S'il fait beau, on prend les vélos.}
Answer a plan with a condition of your own: {Si tu veux, on y va.}

vocabulary.example_fr: La météo dit qu'il va pleuvoir samedi.
vocabulary.example_en: The forecast says it is going to rain on Saturday.

vocabulary.example_fr: S'il fait beau, on prend les vélos.
vocabulary.example_en: If it's nice, we'll take the bikes.

vocabulary.example_fr: S'il pleut, on va à la bibliothèque.
vocabulary.example_en: If it rains, we'll go to the library.

vocabulary.note: Like {pleuvoir}, it only takes {il}: {il neige}, it is snowing.
vocabulary.example_fr: S'il neige, on reste à la maison.
vocabulary.example_en: If it snows, we'll stay at home.

vocabulary.note: Spoken, often with a shrug. It says you are not keen.
vocabulary.example_fr: On va au parc ? Bof, l'herbe est humide.
vocabulary.example_en: Shall we go to the park? Meh, the grass is wet.

concepts.term: {si} + present: a plan that depends on something
concepts.definition: Say the condition with {si} and a verb in the present, then say the plan. The plan can be in the present, with {aller} + infinitive, or an order. The condition stays in the present, even when it is about next Saturday. It can also come after the plan.
concepts.example: {Si tu veux, on y va.} (If you want, let's go.) {Je passe chez toi si j'ai le temps.} (I'll drop by if I have time.)

concepts.definition: {Si} drops its i before {il} and {ils} only. Before {elle}, {on} and every other word, it stays whole.
concepts.example: {s'il pleut}, {s'ils veulent}, {si elle vient}, {si on a le temps}

concepts.definition: After {je ne sais pas} or {je me demande}, {si} means whether. {S'il te plaît} and {s'il vous plaît} mean please.
concepts.example: {Je ne sais pas s'il pleut.} (I don't know whether it's raining.)

items.situation: Léa and Hugo read the weather forecast for Saturday on Léa's phone. Hugo asks: {Qu'est-ce que la météo dit pour samedi ?} Tell him it says it is going to rain.
items.answer: La météo dit qu'il va pleuvoir.
accept: La météo dit qu'il va pleuvoir samedi.
Elle dit qu'il va pleuvoir.
Elle dit qu'il va pleuvoir samedi.
Il va pleuvoir.
Il va pleuvoir samedi.

mistakes.answer: La météo dit que il va pleuvoir.

mistakes.feedback: Keep {va} before the infinitive: {il va pleuvoir}.

items.text: ___ pleut, on va à la bibliothèque.

accept: s'il

items.text: Si tu ___, on prend les vélos.
items.gloss: Léa to Hugo: if you want, we'll take the bikes.

mistakes.feedback: In a real plan, the verb after {si} is in the present: {si tu veux}.
No future after {si}: {si tu veux}, even for Saturday.

mistakes.answer: Si il fait beau, on prend les vélos.

mistakes.answer: S'il va neiger, on reste à la maison.
mistakes.feedback: For the condition, use the present: {s'il neige}. The plan can use {aller}: {on va rester à la maison}.

items.text: Si on ___ le temps, on passe au marché.
items.gloss: Hugo: if we have time, we'll drop by the market.

mistakes.feedback: {Si on avait le temps} goes with {on passerait}, for something you imagine. For a real plan, use the present: {si on a}.

items.text: Si vous ___, on passe samedi. Au revoir, madame !

mistakes.feedback: Léa says {vous} to Mme Garnier, so {si vous voulez}.
